owner_posts.post_text:
SHOULDER DISLOCATION

A shoulder dislocation occurs when the ball of the upper arm bone comes out of its socket completely. 

It can happen after a fall, road traffic accident or during a contact sport. 

Patients experience sudden onset severe pain, difficulty in moving the arm and a visible deformity around the shoulder. 

Emergency care by an orthopaedic surgeon is required as it must be reduced back into its position.

Once the joint is reduced, proper rehabilitation is essential to restore strength and movement. Most of the patients do well later.

Rarely in cases of repeated dislocations, a key-hole arthroscopic surgery is required to repair the torn tissue.

If you are suffering from repeated dislocations of shoulder, consult Dr.Ajinkya Achalare for expert advice and complete orthpedic care.

PLANTAR FASCIITIS 

Heel pain is one of the commonest orthopedic complaints faced by millions of people worldwide and plantar fasciitis is the leading cause.

It can affect anyone who needs to stand or walk for long hours at work or for any other reason.

If you are experiencing persistent heel pain, then this blog will answer many of your doubts.

Click on the following to know more about plantar fasciitis:

Tennis elbow or Lateral Epicondylitis is a common cause of elbow pain.

It is caused by overuse of the forearm muscles and hence the tendons that attach on the outer side of the elbow. 

Despite its name, it does not affect only tennis players but it can affect anyone who performs repetitive gripping, lifting, typing, or wrist movements. 

Symptoms include pain and tenderness on the outer elbow, reduced grip strength, and discomfort while lifting objects or shaking hands. 

Most patients improve with activity modification, ice fomentation, anti-inflammatory medications and stretching exercises. 
Rarely PRP injection and surgery are used as the last resorts.

Early treatment helps prevent chronic pain and allows a quicker return to daily activities and sports.

If you are suffering from constant elbow pain, consult Dr.Ajinkya Achalare for expert orthopedic care.

Jumper’s Knee (Patellar Tendinopathy)

Jumper’s knee is an overuse injury affecting the tendon connecting the knee cap (patella) to the shin bone (tibia). 

It commonly occurs in athletes involved in jumping sports such as basketball, volleyball, and athletics. 

Patients typically experience pain at the front of the knee, especially during jumping, running, squatting, or climbing stairs. 

Early treatment includes activity modification, ice application, and physiotherapy focused on strengthening the quadriceps and tendon. Ignoring symptoms can lead to chronic pain and reduced performance. 

Timely diagnosis and appropriate rehabilitation are essential for a successful recovery.

If you are suffering from similar symptoms, consult Dr.Ajinkya Achalare for an expert orthopedic advice and care.

Para-Meniscal Cyst of Knee: sign of an underlying meniscus tear

A para-meniscal cyst is a fluid-filled swelling that develops next to the meniscus (C-shaped cushion inside the knee joint)

It usually occurs when joint fluid escapes through a small meniscal tear and collects outside the meniscus. 

Patients notice a localised bump near the knee along with pain, tenderness, and discomfort during activities likje walking, climbing stairs. 

MRI is the best investigation to confirm the diagnosis and identify the associated meniscal tear. 

Treatment depends on severity and duration of symptoms and includes medicines & physiotherapy to arthroscopic (key-hole) surgery to repair the underlying meniscus tear and prevent recurrence of the cyst.

If you are suffering from persistent knee pain or a localised swelling along the knee joint, consult Dr.Ajinkya Achalare for an expert orthopedic care.

METATARSALGIA : FOREFOOT PAIN

Metatarsalgia is a common condition causing pain and inflammation in the ball of the foot, usually beneath the metatarsal bones. 

It often develops due to excessive walking, running, high-impact sports, improper footwear, foot deformities, or being overweight. 

Patients typically experience a burning, aching, or sharp pain that worsens while standing or walking and improves with rest. 

Early treatment includes activity modification, orthotic insoles, stretching exercises, and anti-inflammatory medications fora short course. 

However identifying and addressing the underlying cause is essential to prevent chronic symptoms and restore comfortable, pain-free mobility.

If you are suffering from pain over the forefoot, consult Dr.Ajinkya Achalare for best orthopedic advice and care!

WRIST SPRAIN is an injury caused by stretching or tearing of the ligaments that support the wrist joint.

It commonly occurs after a fall on an outstretched hand, twisting injury or lifting weights at the gym or during a sport. 

Symptoms include sudden pain, swelling, bruising, tenderness, and difficulty moving the wrist or gripping objects. 

Immediate care includes rest to the joint, ice application, compression with a crepe bandage, elevation, and temporary splint support. 

Persistent pain and/or swelling beyond 1-2 days should not be ignored and needs urgent medical attention.

If you are have sustained a wrist injury, consult Dr.Ajinkya Achalare at Sphere Clinic, Parel East, Mumbai for expert advice and care.

HYALURONIC ACID INJECTION

A major cause of knee pain in old age is knee osteoarthritis, a degenerative condition in which the smooth cartilage lining of the knee gradually wears out. 

While physiotherapy, weight management, and medications help most of the patients, some continue to have persistent symptoms. 

In such cases, hyaluronic acid injections can be considered as a safe and effective non-surgical treatment option.

If you are suffering from arthritic knee pain, consult Dr.Ajinkya Achalare at Sphere Clinic, Parel for an expert advice and care.

CALCIUM SUPPLEMENTS IN ELDERLY 

- As we age, calcium absorption through gut reduces, increasing the risk of osteoporosis (weak bones) and fractures. 

- In women, this risk further increases due to hormonal changes.

- Elder individuals benefit from calcium supplements when dietary intake is inadequate. 

- The preferred supplements are calcium citrate and calcium carbonate. 

- Calcium citrate is better absorbed in people with low stomach acid and causes less bloating, making it suitable for older adults. 

- Calcium carbonate is economical and works best when taken with meals. 

- Most elderly patients require 1000–1200 mg of elemental calcium daily along with adequate vitamin D for proper absorption. 

- Although excessive calcium intake is hazardous and should be avoided. It is advisable to take supplements only as per your doctor's advice.

- Remember! Calcium supplements are always complementary to a balanced diet and can not replace it.

If you have any further doubts, consult Dr.Ajinkya Achalare at ArthroSports Orthopedic Clinic at Shivaji Park, dadar West, Mumbai for expert opinion and care.

SHOULDER DISLOCATION IN ELDERLY patients commonly occurs after a slip & fall. 

It is typically associated with a fracture of arm bone or a tear of rotator cuff muscle of shoulder. 

Unlike younger individuals, recurrent dislocations is less common, but pain and weakness after the first episode itself are more significant. 

Patients may experience severe shoulder pain, sudden inability to lift the arm, swelling, and deformity around the joint. 

X-rays confirm the diagnosis and rule out fractures. MRI is mandatory to rule out rotator cuff muscle tear.

If you are a middle aged or elderly person with pain & weakness of shoulder, do not ignore the symptoms.

featured_reviews.name: Aditi Pathare
featured_reviews.review_text:
After looking at the 5-star reviews, I visited this doctor for my mother’s left leg pain. Unfortunately, our experience was disappointing. The doctor is polite in speech but seems very money-minded.

During the first visit, he charged ₹1500 (normal fees), but strongly insisted on getting a Doppler test done through a specific lab. He even called the lab in front of us and mentioned sending the patient directly, which clearly felt like a commission-based referral. This was despite us clearly stating that we wanted to do the test at another known place. He claimed that ultrasounds done elsewhere would not be reliable. The lab he suggested charged ₹6000, while we got the same test done at our known place for ₹5000.

As instructed, we shared the report with him on WhatsApp, but there was no response. Later, my brother personally visited the clinic just to show the reports (the patient was not present). Ideally, this should have been free since it was only for report discussion, but he still charged ₹1000. On top of that, he again recommended another radiologist by sharing a specific name and phone number.

Overall, this was the most money-minded and disappointing experience I’ve had with a doctor.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Hello! I really feel sorry for patients like you.It is unfortunate that when a correct clinical diagnosis was made and appropriate steps were taken to prevent you from being misled, the response is criticism rather than appreciation. You previously did an incorrect scan elsewhere, which you don't have anything to say about. Now, when a correct scan was suggested after clinical examination, and a correct diagnosis was made, here you are making allegations without even having visited for the follow up consultation and understanding the problem. Let's get the facts clear!

The reason a specific centre was suggested, was to prevent a repeat of an incorrect investigation (like you did before). Prior to consulting me, a venous Doppler had already been done, while your mother’s clinical presentation was not sciatica or venous problem, but strongly suggestive of arterial insufficiency (ischemic pain). A venous Doppler would never diagnose this condition.

The recommendation was therefore for a proper arterial Doppler, done by a senior, reliable radiologist, with whom precise requirements could be clearly communicated. The phone call was made only to ensure the correct study was performed this time — not for any financial reason. I have no commission arrangements, nor do I compel patients to visit any particular center. You were always free to choose where to do the test, which you ultimately did — and the scan confirmed the arterial block, exactly as suspected clinically. (which you should rather appreciate for spot on clinical diagnosis!)

Suggesting accuracy over repetition of wrong tests is called responsible medical practice, not “money-mindedness”.

At no point were you instructed to seek treatment or consultation over WhatsApp. Medical opinions are not given casually over messages.

Your brother later visited the clinic for formal report discussion and guidance, which constitutes a consultation. Doctors do not charge for “presence of the patient” — they charge for professional expertise, time, and responsibility involved in interpreting reports and guiding next steps. This is the same principle by which professionals in any field are paid for their work. Do you or your family members work for free? or ever say to your boss that you don't want payment for a particular month? or a 50% less salary this month would be okay?

If there was any financial difficulty, it could have been communicated. We offer concessions, fee waivers, and charity OPD options for genuinely needy patients. We doctors do that.

It is disappointing that sincere efforts to guide a patient onto the correct diagnostic path are interpreted otherwise. Medicine requires trust in clinical judgment, not assumptions about intent.

I genuinely wish your mother good health. However, when decision-makers are like you who lack trust and respect for sound medical advice, it may indeed be better to continue with whose approach you are more comfortable with and keep on doing investigation after investigations. All the best! 👍🏻

We categorically deny the allegations and the language used in this review.

Osteoporosis is diagnosed using standardized DEXA scan criteria (T-scores), which are objective and machine-generated. In this case, DEXA scans done at two different centres( Nirman and Divine - both independent,  reputed centres ) two years apart, showed similar findings, confirming low bone density - this indicates consistency rather than error. 

It is also relevant that you had already received bone-strengthening injectable treatment from a previous doctor, which is prescribed only when osteoporosis or significant bone loss is established.

The repeat DEXA scan was advised only to address your doubts and was facilitated at a discounted rate, not to influence results. Diagnostic centres operate independently, and doctors neither control nor alter scan readings.

At no point was any daily injection costing ₹1 lakh per year prescribed. Treatment options, were explained as optional and as per standard guidelines, and you were encouraged to seek a third opinion — which is every patient’s right.

While we respect differing opinions, abusive language, false claims, and personal attacks are unacceptable. Posting misleading conclusions about standard diagnostic tests and using offensive language towards healthcare professionals is inappropriate and unwarranted. 

We remain available for factual discussion but will not engage in defamatory accusations.
